resources.string: TCU Screenomics: Linking Human Digital Phenotyping with Mental Health

You are invited to participate in a research study. To participate, you must be:

(1) Able to see and hear clearly
(2) Able to speak and read English fluently
(3) Living in the United States
(4) At least 18 years old, but not older than 25 years old
(5) The sole user of an Android smartphone (not shared)
(6) An active user of at least 2 social media accounts

This study is being conducted online and at Room 213, Winton-Scott Hall, Texas Christian University (TCU). It is an observational study designed to understand daily digital behaviors among young adults (ages 18–25) using multimodal passive sensing markers combining physiological signals, smartphone screenshots, and brief self-report surveys.

You will be one of 60 participants at TCU. Your participation is voluntary. You may withdraw at any time. We will maintain the confidentiality of your information.
What is the purpose of the research?

The purpose of this study is to understand how young adults use digital devices and how daily smartphone habits and physical signals (heart rate, sleep, activity) are connected to mental health and overall wellbeing.

We hope to identify digital and physical patterns that signal changes in mood, stress levels, and mental health symptoms to support early detection and personalized care.

Participants are asked to:
(1) Install the Screenomics app, which passively captures screenshots every five seconds while the phone is in use.
(2) Install the Centralive app to complete EMA surveys approximately four times per day over 28 days.
(3) Wear a Garmin vivosmart 5 wearable device continuously throughout the study (except during charging).
What are the risks and how will they be minimized?

This study involves moderate risks, higher than minimal.

1. Psychological Risk (Sensitive Surveys):
Surveys include mental health questions that may cause mild discomfort. You may skip any question or opt out at any time without consequences.

Mental health resources:
• TCU Counseling Center: 817-257-7863
• 24/7 Helpline: 817-257-7233
• National Suicide and Crisis Lifeline: Call or Text 988

2. Time Burden:
Less than 8 minutes of active survey time per day. Onboarding takes 30–60 minutes. End-of-study survey takes approximately 150 minutes (2.5 hours).

3. Cognitive Burden:
Managing apps and the Garmin device for 28 days requires sustained attention. The research team is available for technical support throughout the study.

4. Privacy Risk (Screen Monitoring):
Screenshots are captured every five seconds while your phone is in use. You may pause or resume recording at any time through the app. Less than 1% of screenshots will be viewed manually by trained TCU researchers. All data is encrypted and stored on secure, password-protected TCU servers. You may request removal of your data at any time.

1. Onboarding (Room 213 or Zoom):
Review this consent form, install the Screenomics and Centralive apps, and receive your Garmin wearable device.

2. Questionnaires (online):
Complete a 150-minute baseline survey at the start, brief 2-minute EMA surveys four times per day for 28 days, and a 150-minute end-of-study survey. You may skip any question you do not want to answer.

3. Fitness Tracker:
Wear the Garmin device continuously for 28 days to passively record sleep, heart rate, activity, and stress (except during charging).

4. Post-Study Feedback Interviews:
Attend 2 individual and 2 group interviews (Room 213 or Zoom) to share your experience and help refine the study.

The Screenomics app records anything on your screen including home screens, websites, photos, and messages. You may pause recording or withdraw at any time. We will not provide clinical diagnoses or treatment recommendations.

Confidentiality:
Your data will be labeled by study ID number, not your name. All data is encrypted and stored on secure TCU servers. De-identified Screenomics data will be retained for up to 10 years. De-identified non-screenomic data will be kept indefinitely for future research.

Limits of Confidentiality:
If information suggests serious concern about your well-being or safety of others, we may be required to report to appropriate authorities (e.g., information relating to suicide or abuse).

Compensation (up to $165 total):
• $2.50/day for passive sensing and EMA completion
• $10 bonus for completing any 14 days of EMA
• $15 bonus for completing all 28 days of EMA
• $15 for completing the baseline survey
• $15 for completing the end-of-study survey
• $10 per feedback interview (up to 4 interviews)

There are no costs to you for participating.
